doc.title: Albert Warner and Sonny Henry Interview, 1959-01-08

title: Christening, school and church music in boyhood
summary: Warner recalls his church, the Robertson school, singing lessons from charts and organs and melodeons in church.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: See, I forgot to ask you why you were christened at.
I was christened at the oldest church in here, that's St. Boniface, Catholic. Well, that church now is not even in existence. It was back on Yalvis, Yalvis and Onsaga.
Oh, yeah. Yeah. And where did you go to school here?
Yeah. The Robertson School. The Robertson School. I first went to By Road School down at... Durbany and Governor Nicholas. Well, they used to call it By Road Street then, back in those days, you see?
Governor Nicholas was called By Road?

Yeah. Back in those days, it was By Road Street, you see? Now they called it Governor Nicholas. Well, that was an old break building was there. Now they got a new school there, you see. All new school there. See, well, way back in that time they had all white teachers in there. Mm-hmm. Well, after they moved us from there, they moved us up to Bienville and Robertson, old Robertson School, across from the cemetery. These were public schools? Public schools, yeah. See, then from that school, and then that's where they tore this, tore that school down, they built up the one on Bienville Street, they called it the Wicker School. Wicker School, that's old Robertson School. Mm-hmm. See? That's way back in 19... 1910. So, no further back than that. 1903. 1903. I wasn't here then. Yeah. Did you have a band at school? No, they didn't. They used to teach you music, but they didn't have any bands. They wasn't teaching you music in school. All they did was teach you the notes and things, you know?
I had a great big... Yeah. They used to learn you how to sing. They had a great big... The blackboard, yeah.

Oh, you know, like them great big sheets, you know? Mm-hmm. Oh, yeah. them great big sheets you know and they had notes and things on there, learn your different notes and they'd throw that sheet over and get the next lesson if they had. It was just the same like, you know like they used to have some of these Sunday schools, Sunday they'd like to have those lessons on, they'd throw them sheets over, yeah that's what it was like you see, that's the way they used to learn you how to read music, but it didn't have any teaching the bands or anything, teaching the bands that just come up here lately, taking the long yard to play music in these schools. What did they have in the churches now?
Did they have an organ in the church or a piano or any instrument? Well back, you mean way back
in time, in the olden time? Well no, most of it was organs, they didn't have no pianos

that I know of, and what about in the country? Well they didn't have no piano or nothing to your voice, you know. See back, you had to get out there and tough it up, you understand? With your voice, everybody would get together, you understand, and sing together. See they

used to call them melodians, they was a red big thing and they had like pipes, you know, come up, and they had small one and then they'd go right on straight on up, some as long as what he is there. See they had like hole cut in them like, like them flutes, them flutes that you used to call them melodians. In the later years they started calling them organ, pipe organs. Well then they'd have a fella back there, he'd be there pumping the thing while the organist would be playing, you see, but he'd be back there, he'd be pumping there. See, as long as she's playing well he just had to stay there and pump. I used to do that thing. You did it too? Well then you know what I'm talking about, you know what I'm talking about, what they call the melodians, huh? Well this is a pipe organ. Pipe organ, right, pipe organ, yeah, they had them big pipes there. I didn't know you were a musician. Uh-uh, uh-uh, uh-uh. You didn't know he was a violin? He was a musician. He was pumping his way through. You know what I was talking about, eh? You just was listening and you'd find out what I was talking about. That old fella used to be back there, man, he had that poor handle, sometime you see he'd be weak back there. You see him pumping there, but he kept pumping till his top. Yeah.
